segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They did it for twenty minutes, all of them, wards and Embers and still doors alike, in pairs across the dock floor in the grey light, letting go of a rope's end into the air above an open hand and not looking to see if it was caught. Kiva did it with Pru, and then with Hesketh, and then with the elder Pascoe, who let go of it very carefully as though it might break. It was absurd. It was the most useful twenty minutes of the day. By the end of it, when Kiva called nobody over the tun, every ward on the plank opened on the end of the word, together, and the tun hung on nothing for the space of a quarter of a count before the Embers had it, and it did not slop at all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At half past four they ran it end to end three times, on the dry floor, with the tun, from one chalk mark to the next and the next and the next. On the third run Kiva found that she was not saying nobody the way she had said it at Mallow, short, with the swallow, to two people who had rehearsed it with her on a yard. She was saying it louder, and longer, and from her stomach, so that a girl from Holloway twelve paces off with her back half turned would hear it at the same instant as Anwen at her elbow. It was a different word when eighteen people had to hear it at once. It had to be a word that belonged to nobody's ear in particular.
